title: Graveyard shift - handoff quicknotes (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight scratchpad for graveyard/on-call handoffs. Not a polished runbook yet — things here are quick commands, heuristics that helped me, and TODOs for the formal runbook. Use at your discretion; double-check before running anything that touches production clusters.

High-level goals for the shift
- Keep inference latency P95 < 350ms for hosted-api-primary region.
- Prevent noisy autoscaler thrash on dedicated pools.
- Keep errors from hitting customer-facing routes (tiered fallbacks enabled).

Quick handoff checklist (what I care about)
- Incidents open: note IDs and status (below)
- Current active deploys/rollouts? (check CI / release slack)
- Any capacity alerts (GPU pods OOM / node-drain scheduled)
- Anything requiring immediate pager escalation (pager rules in Confluence link)

Current state snapshot (as of start of my shift)
- Hosted API: healthy, 99.8% success in last hour, small spike 02:12 UTC (investigating).
- Dedicated pool: pool-ded-xx running at 82% utilization, one pod on restart loop but in backoff (see incident INF-2026-07).
- Private deployments: no active tickets.
- Recent rollouts: model-mix-v2 canary 20% -> no regressions flagged.

Immediate triage steps (for incoming pager: high token error rate / model timeouts)
1) Confirm if customer-facing or internal test: check request IDs from logs -> https://logs.internal/reqlookup?req={REQUEST_ID} 
2) Check host metrics: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "model-mix|runtime" ; kubectl logs POD -c runtime --since=10m
3) Check model runtime traces: go to tracing ui -> filter by route /model/stream-gen and sample traces with latency > 1s.
4) If GPU OOM or repeated model crashes: scale down batch size / switch to fallback model:
   - To trigger fallback routing: POST https://admin.internal/api/routing/fallback 
     body: {"route":"/text/generate", "fallback_model":"mix-small-quant"} (ops token required)
   - If you cannot reach admin API, patch deployment: kubectl patch deploy runtime-mix -p '\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"spec\":{\"containers\":[{\"name\":\"runtime\",\"env\":[{\"name\":\"FORCE_FALLBACK\",\"value\":\"1\"}]}]}}}'
5) If autoscaler thrash (rapid scale up/down): temporarily disable scale down window: kubectl annotate hpa inference-hpa alpha.autoscaling.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=\"true\" --overwrite

Commands I used tonight (copy/paste friendly)
- View error spikes last 2h: curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?m=error_rate&range=2h" | jq .
- Restart a misbehaving runtime pod safely: kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-mix -n inference --timeout=5m
- Force a canary rollback: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${OPS_TOKEN}' -d '{"canary":false}' https://deploy.internal/api/canary/model-mix-v2

Temporary procedures (quick, not yet formalized)
- If host network is flapping in a single AZ -> move traffic to secondary region (manual routing):
  1) Toggle weight to region-us-west-2 via admin UI (Traffic > Routes).
  2) Monitor P50/P95 for 15 minutes; revert when stable.
- If KV cache pressure causes token generation slowdowns -> clear small shards first:
  redis-cli -h kv-cache-host CLUSTER CALL FLUSHDB (DO NOT RUN WITHOUT OPS APPROVAL for full cluster flush)

Unresolved items / followups for runbook
- Formalize 'fallback routing' API usage and create safe wrapper script for on-call (remove manual kubectl patch step).
- Add playbook for autoscaler thrash with clear thresholds and rollback steps.
- Add step-by-step for moving traffic between regions with screenshots.
- Confirm whether model-mix-v2 has a staged quantized variant for low-memory fallback.

Notes to next on-call (Harper -> whoever)
- I left INF-2026-07 in progress: one pod in pool-ded-xx restarted 5x; I throttled canary to 10% and opened the ticket. Monitor for more restarts; if >3 restarts in 15m escalate to oncall-2.
- If you get a latency alert and nothing obvious in logs, try toggling FORCE_PREFETCH=0 on runtime as a temporary toggle (reduces memory pressure but increases CPU).

Quick escalation matrix
- Oncall-1 (night): page pager1 -> follow steps above
- Oncall-2 (senior): page pager2 -> escalate for infra/cluster issues or customer-impacting regressions
- Engineering manager: page EM if incident exceeds 4 hours or requires cross-team coordination

Personal reminders (handy tips I found)
- When investigating high cold-start latencies, check KVM hostiops and GPU driver logs (nvidia-smi dmon) — sometimes node-level jitter is upstream of runtime.
- Use 'trace sampling' in tracing UI with tag "sample:oncall" to avoid losing helpful traces.

TODOs (for me)
- [ ] Turn this into a proper runbook section under Confluence by end of next sprint.
- [ ] Add scripted fallback toggle with a safe revert flag.
- [ ] Write postmortem template for recurrent pod restart loops.

Random troubleshooting snippets (notes-to-self)
- Found a weird 502 pattern once due to a misconfigured nginx timeout: check nginx/proxy timeouts if you see upstream reset and no pod OOM.
- If you suspect overload but CPU is low, check queue depth on request broker (rabbitmq/stolon) — sometimes backpressure is upstream.

End of notes. Ping me on slack (harper.nguyen) if anything breaks or if you want a quick walkthrough of the steps.
